Estimate the effect at each level of a grouping, with partial pooling

Source: R/cate.R
pollin_cate.Rd

Reads the estimand's contrast at each level of a column that carries a random treatment slope: the unit column of the design's slope (pollin_design(slope = ), a slope on the outermost unit), or the column declared with pollin_fit(pooled = ). Each level's effect is formed by G-computation over the rows at that level, every row keeping its random effects, so a level with little data is pulled towards the overall effect.

Usage

pollin_cate(fit, by = NULL, conf_level = 0.95, n = 4000L, seed = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A pollin_fit() object with a random treatment slope.

by

The column whose levels are reported. NULL (the default) takes the fit's pooled column, or else the unit column of the design's slope.

conf_level

Level of the interval.

n

Number of draws for the interval.

seed

Optional seed for the draws. The session's random number state is restored afterwards.

Value

An object of class pollin_cate: a list holding table, with one row per response and level and the columns response, contrast, level, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, pooled (TRUE), n (rows of the model data at the level), family, scale, basis, distribution and interval ("conditional" on glmmTMB, "posterior" on flexyBayes); and by, engine, conf_level, n, seed and the estimand.

Details

On the glmmTMB engine the estimate uses the fixed effects and the conditional modes of the random effects. The interval is approximate: the fixed and random effects are drawn jointly from a multivariate normal with the covariance of the delta interval of pollin_effects() (the inverse of the joint precision of the Laplace approximation); it is the percentile interval of the effects recomputed per draw, and std.error their standard deviation. On the flexyBayes engine the effects come from the posterior draws of pollin_draws(): the estimate is their median and the interval their equal-tailed interval.

The table holds pooled contrasts only. A fit that pools a column does not also fit its levels as fixed effects, so the unpooled per-level contrasts come from a second fit, pollin_fit(estimand, by = ) without the slope on that column, read with pollin_effects(); the two side by side show what the pooling moved. The print names which table is which.

See also

pollin_effects() for the trial contrast and the fixed per-level contrasts.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(3)
d <- data.frame(
  trt = rep(rep(c("Cage", "Open"), each = 8L), 12L),
  Site = rep(sprintf("s%02d", seq_len(12L)), each = 16L)
)
slope <- rnorm(12L, 0, 0.3)[as.integer(factor(d$Site))]
d$pods <- rnbinom(
  nrow(d),
  mu = exp(3 + (0.3 + slope) * (d$trt == "Open")),
  size = 20
)
pd <- pollin_data(d, "pods", "trt", unit = "Site")
ds <- pollin_design(pd, c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"), "multi_site")
est <- pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "ratio", "loss")
pollin_cate(pollin_fit(est), n = 1000L, seed = 1L)

if (requireNamespace("flexyBayes", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit_b <- pollin_fit(est, engine = "flexyBayes")
  pollin_cate(fit_b, n = 1000L, seed = 1L)
}
#> flexyBayes: by default the residual and each random-effect standard deviation have a half_normal(scale = 3) prior, on the log scale of the mean, with the scale divided by sd(x) for a random slope on x.
